speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a)what have been done to control the population of wild birds in HDB estates and the possible transmission of diseases by birds; and (b) whether methods used by airports such as a sonic system to chase away the birds can be used to prevent the birds from over-growing in HDB estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Second, AVA also works with the National Environment Agency (NEA) and Town Councils to ensure proper disposal of food waste at our hawker centres and within our residential areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This reduces the availability of food that will attract the birds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Third, AVA also works with NParks and Town Councils to prune trees within the estates to deter birds from roosting in those trees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: AVA also inspects pet shops that sell birds to the general public to ensure that the birds are properly looked after and in good health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Moreover, in our farming industry, our local poultry farms are required to put in place proper biosecurity measures to prevent any disease incursion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Members of the public are advised therefore also to exercise due care and caution to not handle any dead birds or have direct contact with bird droppings because these are where diseases can be transmitted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Such sonic systems can also be quite loud which reduces their suitability for deployment in our dense residential areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The public, I must emphasise, also has an important role to play in curbing the bird population by maintaining the overall cleanliness of the environment and not feeding the wild birds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: AVA, NEA and Town Councils will continue to educate residents not to litter or feed the birds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Enforcement actions will be taken against those who do not comply.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In my area, we have areas that despite the joint efforts put in, the issue is not solved.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, I want to know besides those methods that the Senior Minister of State has mentioned, are there any other latest methods that could be used to resolve this issue?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In fact, I have one case which is quite bad.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When I was there I can see it is noisy.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is it possible to change to another type of tree whereby it will deter birds from resting in these trees?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I know there are some blocks in which we have residents throwing food particles, food substances out from the kitchen window.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These are behaviour that constitutes the source of attraction for the birds to come.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And once the birds are used to coming to a certain location because of the availability of food, they will then find natural places to roost.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I think in tackling this issue, it is not about deploying more and more technology.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: AVA adopts a science-based approach to see which of these methods can be an effective way to deter the birds.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But no scientific method will deter birds from coming back to sources of food.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is where we need to continue to strengthen our public education, to also take enforcement actions where necessary against people who throw food particles out of their windows.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They continue to constitute a source of attraction for the birds.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I would say it is not just more methods.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Some of these methods can be expensive and with very limited efficacy over a period of time.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In the longer run, it is always more cost-effective and more durable if you work at the source of it which is to deter uncivil behaviour.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And also to make sure that our food establishment in our estates continue to practise good habits, good practices of removing food wastes.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: From the resident who gave me the feedback, I also understand that there was no throwing of food, no high-rise littering to attract birds.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: From the feedback I gathered, it is because the birds know where to source for the food.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: In fact, they fly into the house, fly into the flat whenever the residents prepare a nice dinner or nice lunch on the dining table.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: The Senior Minister of State is right; that could be the source but we cannot really ask everybody to close their windows.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think there are certain trees in which birds may be attracted to, especially those that could be fruiting.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong, do you have a clarification to make?
